title: HelperSSHVerifyHostKeyParams
description: The helper asking what to make of a host key it was just offered. It has no other way to find out: the helper links no knownhosts — a forbidden import in the deployed artifact (internal/helper/deploy/dependency_test.go) — and it must not decide for itself whether an unseen key may be accepted, because that decision is a question for a person. It carries TWO addresses because the key is offered for one and STORED under another: a host reached through a jump host is recorded under an opaque digest the coordinator computes, and the offered address is what a person is shown.

host.description: The address the key was OFFERED for: the address this helper dialed. It is what the verdict's error and its evidence name, and what the accept sheet shows a person.

knownHostsAddr.description: The STORAGE identity the coordinator looks the key up under, when it differs from the offered address. A direct route records its key under its own address, and this is empty there; a route through a jump host records it under an opaque digest that only the coordinator can compute (ssh_real.go's knownHostsTargetAddr), so the value is the coordinator's — the helper echoes what the destination carried — and a helper that derived one would look for a line the next connection would not find.

algorithm.description: The offered key's own type string, as the helper read it off the handshake. It is checked against the key bytes, so a disagreement between the two ends about WHICH key this is becomes a refusal rather than a fingerprint of a key nobody asked about.

key.description: The wire-format public key blob the peer presented (RFC 4253 §6.6), base64. Public material: it is what the peer sends on the first packet of every handshake.
